Did NOT add a DELETE route. The Figma state set for M08 (Default/Loading/Empty/Error/Create Rule/Invalid Regex/Disable Confirmation/Mobile) has no delete affordance or confirmation dialog — the only designed destructive-ish action is Disable (reversible, non-destructive to Finding data), matching scopeNotes in this file. Regex validation: pattern must be non-empty and must compile via `new RegExp(pattern)` (InvalidPatternError -> 409 otherwise). Also added a cheap heuristic rejection of classic catastrophic-backtracking shapes (nested quantifiers like (a+)+, (a*)*, (x{2,})+) — intentionally a shape check, not a full static ReDoS analyzer, per the task's explicit 'do not over-engineer' instruction.

findings.title: ReDoS: worker had no regex execution timeout; admin-side heuristic guard was bypassable
findings.description: apps/worker/src/rules/engine.ts ran new RegExp(pattern).exec(snippet) synchronously against untrusted scanned GitHub content with no timeout. The original hasCatastrophicBacktrackingShape() heuristic in lib/scanRules.ts only caught nested-quantifier shapes (e.g. (a+)+), missing quantified-alternation shapes (e.g. (a|aa)+b), which was empirically confirmed to cause 8+ seconds of exponential backtracking on a 36-character adversarial input — reachable by any admin account (or hijacked admin session) and capable of hanging the scanner worker indefinitely, blocking scanning for all customers, not just the attacker's own rule.
findings.fix: Two changes: (1) apps/web/lib/scanRules.ts's assertValidPattern now also rejects quantified-alternation shapes ((a|aa)+ style) and caps pattern length at 500 chars, as a stronger but still best-effort admin-input filter. (2) The actual security boundary: apps/worker/src/rules/engine.ts's evaluateRule now delegates match execution to a new apps/worker/src/rules/safe-exec.ts, which runs regex.exec on a dedicated, disposable worker_thread with a hard 250ms wall-clock budget (excluding one-time thread cold-start, tracked separately via a workerReady promise). A pattern that misses the budget is treated as a non-match (fail closed) and its stuck thread is terminated and replaced on the next call — regex.exec cannot be interrupted mid-call any other way in Node. This guarantees no pattern, regardless of shape or origin (including any pre-existing DB row written before the stronger heuristic existed), can hang the scanner beyond ~250ms per evaluation. evaluateRule/evaluateAllRules became async; the one caller (scanner.worker.ts) and the existing test suite (rules-engine.test.ts) were updated accordingly, plus a new adversarial-input test asserting the (a|aa)+b pattern resolves to null well within a generous bound instead of hanging.
